title: Inferring the Unspoken: Aligning Embodied Agents with Implicit Preferences
abstract: arXiv:2502.00858v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Natural-language instructions rarely specify every detail required for embodied action. An agent asked to ``prepare an apple,'' for example, must still determine whether to wash or cut it, where to place it, and in what order to perform these actions. Such decisions often reflect user-specific preferences that are demonstrated through behavior but never explicitly stated. We study whether embodied agents can infer these latent preferences from a small number of prior demonstrations and apply them when planning in new situations. To support systematic evaluation, we introduce Preference-based Planning (PbP), a benchmark containing 5,000 evaluation groups and 290 preferences organized into three levels: atomic action parameters, strategic interaction and placement policies, and temporal ordering constraints. translated_title: 推断未言之意：将具身智能体与内隐偏好对齐
translated_abstract: 自然语言指令很少能明确指定具身行动所需的全部细节。例如，被要求“准备一个苹果”的智能体，仍需决定是清洗还是切苹果、将其放置在哪里，以及按何种顺序执行这些操作。这些决策往往反映了用户特有的偏好，这类偏好通过行为表现出来，却从未被明确陈述。我们研究具身智能体能否从少量先验示范中推断出这些潜在偏好，并在新情境规划时加以应用。为支持系统性评估，我们提出了基于偏好的规划基准，该基准包含5,000个评估组和290个偏好，分为三个层次：原子动作参数、策略性交互与放置策略，以及时序排序约束。我们进一步提出了InTU（Inferring the Unspoken），一个两阶段框架，该框架首先将从多模（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出了PbP基准和InTU两阶段框架，使具身智能体能够从少量示范中推断用户未言明的内隐偏好，并将其应用于新情境下的任务规划。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the PbP benchmark and the InTU two-stage framework, enabling embodied agents to infer users' unspoken implicit preferences from a small number of demonstrations and apply them when planning in new situations.
